name: 王可
objective:
Explore the systems behind everyday life, explain sustainability concepts in English, and try a meaningful sustainability action. Students evaluate information, discuss issues, lead classmates in an activity, and reflect on the relationship between individual action and larger systems.

Learning Objectives
1. Recognize how everyday life is shaped by larger social and environmental systems.
2. Use English to explain a sustainability issue, evaluate information, and lead an activity that helps others discuss and learn about the issue.
3. Experiment with one meaningful sustainability action and reflect on what it reveals about the system behind it.
schedule:
Week 1: Introduction to systems
Week 2: Misinformation
Week 3: Debunking Misinformation
Week 4: No class (Teachers’ Day)
Week 5: Consumption and Waste
Week 6: Consumption and Waste II; introduction to Sustainability Playground
Week 7: Model facilitation: Accessibility
Week 8: No class (Taiwan Retrocession Day observed)
Week 9: Student-led facilitation, Groups 1–2; sustainability experiment introduction
Week 10: No class (University Anniversary)
Week 11: Student-led facilitation, Groups 3–4
Week 12: Student-led facilitation, Groups 5–6
Week 13: Student-led facilitation, Groups 7–8
Week 14: Student-led facilitation, Groups 9–10
Week 15: Student-led facilitation, Groups 11–12
Week 16: Sustainability experiment sharing with Q&A
Changes to dates and deadlines will be announced in advance.
scorePolicy:
Participation & In-Class Work: 30%
Sustainability Playground: 10%
Sustainability Experiment: 20%
Speaking performance: 10% (regular class reporting 2%, Sustainability Playground 4%, experiment report 4%)
Writing performance: 10% (class writing 5%, experiment proposal 5%)
University English midterm common exam (listening and reading): 20%

Speaking evidence comes from at least three individual performances across class reports, facilitation, and experiment sharing. Writing evidence includes the experiment proposal, revised after teacher feedback, and final reflection. Common ESP rubrics apply. A CEFR B2-or-higher result in Speaking or Writing from BESTEP or another recognized test gives full credit for the corresponding 10% component. Without B2, students earn the grade through course assessments. All students participate in speaking and writing activities.

AI permissions are specified for each task; AI must not replace students’ language practice, independent thinking, or judgment.

延伸教學與資源:
● 參與式創新教學 (Participatory & Innovative Teaching)
強調學生參與與產出，導入翻轉、PBL/專題、設計思考或遊戲化等策略。
Emphasizes student engagement and outcomes by adopting strategies such as Flipped Classroom, PBL (Problem/Project- Based Learning), Design Thinking, or Gamification.
● 數位教材資源應用 (Application of Digital Resources)
採用影音多媒體或具開放授權之資源（如 OCW、開放教科書）作為主要或輔助教材。
Adopts multimedia or open-licensed resources (e.g., OCW, Open Textbooks) as primary or supplementary teaching materials.
